subject: fix(interactive): a missing mount is not a verdict on a checkpointed turn
instruction:
fix(interactive): a missing mount is not a verdict on a checkpointed turn

`recover_checkpointed_dispatch/2` marked a turn ambiguous on any
`authorize_turn_attachments/2` failure. For an attachment-level failure that is honest —
the named file is gone or outside the workspace, so the checkpointed input cannot be
reproduced. `{:invalid_attachment_workspace, reason}` is different: the workspace *root*
failed to canonicalize, which is infrastructure, and the turn is still exactly
reproducible once the root is back. It now takes the same bounded backoff an unreachable
`Session.info/1` takes, instead of permanently burning a turn over a mount that was not
up yet.

Recovery reports its outcome to `refresh_session/1` rather than returning a runtime, so a
retry short-circuits the pipeline the way every other retry does — checkpointing session
info on top of it would have discarded the backoff it just scheduled.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - a checkpointed attachment that cannot exist burns its turn, a missing root does not

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends, applied to a fresh checkout of the starting commit. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place, but they are yours: they are not copied into the tree the grade runs in. The change is collected as a diff over `lib/`, `assets/`, `priv/`, `config/`, `docs/` and `README.md`; a change to any other path — `mix.exs` and `.formatter.exs` included — is refused rather than graded. Work only inside this worktree.
